relevance.rationale: The folio's 13-driver menu carries driver (x) as a 'MacMahon-style partition-algebra count' (conj:kashaev-density-equals-sdp-multiplicity, and computations/probes/h4_categorical_drivers_probe.py which computes a MacMahon-master-theorem value at H_4). That driver is currently a menu label with no literature theorem behind it. This paper is exactly that theorem: it derives the colored Jones function from the q-MacMahon Master Theorem as the inverse of a non-commutative fermionic determinant. It does not close any QOU gap by itself -- the folio's driver (x) is about a partition-algebra COUNT at H_4, not about a knot-diagram arc-graph -- so it is background/technique, not a load-bearing input.

keyResults.statement: For every knot diagram K, J_n(K,q) = q^{delta(K,n)} / Ferm(B'_K) n-evaluated, where Ferm(A) = sum over subsets J of (-1)^{|J|} det_q(A_J) is the alternating sum of quantum minors and B'_K is the arc-graph matrix.
keyResults.useForFolio: Supplies the literature link the corpus's driver (x) asserts but does not source: the MacMahon/boson-fermion mechanism is what produces the colored Jones, so a MacMahon-style partition count is not an arbitrary menu entry. Cite it where driver (x) is introduced.

keyResults.statement: Delta(K,t) = t*det(I - B_K) at q=1 (the same matrix, specialised), and consequently lim_n J_n(K, q^{1/n}) = 1/Delta(K,q) (Melvin-Morton-Rozansky).
keyResults.useForFolio: One matrix yielding both Alexander and colored Jones -- the determinant/Alexander degeneration that also appears in Murakami math/0405126 eq. (1.1) and in the corpus's Alexander-polynomial usage (shell-threading-conjecture, torsion-knot-flow). Useful as the structural explanation for why the abelian branch produces 1/Delta.
